title: Factors in Determination of Value of Land for Public and Private Housing
what_it_is: Factors in Determination of Value of Land for Public and Private Housing

sections.label: Valuing land for HDB BTO flats
sections.summary: Asked what differential the Chief Valuer applies to public housing land versus private housing land, and whether private housing land comparables are used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in determining the value of land that will be used to build HDB BTO flats (a) what is the differential that the Chief Valuer applies to land used for public housing compared to that for private housing; and (b) whether the private housing land use comparables used to value land for HDB BTO flats are based on the records of the last transacted private residential land sold by the Government and private parties.

sections.label: Chief Valuer determines HDB land value
sections.summary: HDB pays fair market value set by the Chief Valuer; private housing land transactions are not used, and public housing land premiums are lower.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Instead, the fair market value that HDB must pay for the purchase of state land for public housing is independently determined by the Chief Valuer using well accepted and established valuation principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Transactions pertaining to land sold for private housing developments are not used to value the land sold to HDB for public housing developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: On the differential, which is also the Member's question, HDB has publicly stated that the land premium paid for public housing land parcels is lower than the premiums for equivalent land used for private housing, as observed from the returns of successful tender bids by private developers through GLS.

sections.label: Leong Mun Wai historical cost proposal
sections.summary: Leong Mun Wai said in public that state land sold to HDB should be valued at historical acquisition cost rather than professional valuation principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Relevant to this topic raised by Mr Giam are the recent comments made by Mr Leong Mun Wai in the public domain, where he said that state land sold to HDB should instead be valued at the historical cost of acquisition rather than on professional valuation principles which I have just articulated.

sections.label: Alleged raid on national reserves
sections.summary: The speaker says Leong Mun Wai is seeking to raid national reserves by promising cheap HDB flats without more taxes or other revenue sources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It sounds like it, but it is not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: He is in fact seeking to raid our national reserves in promising you that he can make HDB flats dirt cheap – but better, without having to tax Singaporeans more or to find ways to pay for it through revenue sources.

sections.label: HDB must pay fair market value
sections.summary: HDB must put the fair market value of state land back into the reserves; paying historical price would put back far less and diminish reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: While Government cannot touch the proceeds from land sales which go to the reserves and are then re-invested, part of the growth in value of our reserves, the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC), is used to fund today's needs such as healthcare, housing, subsidies, security and so on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, when state land is sold to HDB, HDB must put back into the reserves the fair market value (FMV) of the land, turn the land that is in our reserves into its equivalent value of money at this point in time, so the reserves are not worse-off or diminished.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Mr Leong's proposal for HDB to pay historical price to the reserves means putting back into the reserves far less than what the state land is really worth today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This is a raid on the reserves, plain and simple, and will diminish the resources available for your children and their children.

sections.label: Populist approach to reserves
sections.summary: The speaker says the approach is populist: sell land to HDB at historical cost, ignoring market valuation, for cheap housing without more taxes or cutbacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, instead, the approach is the populist one – raid our reserves, but do not say it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: He says Government can sell land to HDB at distant historical cost and ignore market valuation principles, so that Singaporeans today can get dirt cheap housing without having to pay more taxes or experience cutbacks elsewhere to pay for this.

sections.label: Deal sounds too good
sections.summary: The speaker says most people would recognise the proposed deal sounds too good to be true.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Then, we can have a sound, fair basis for discussion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But the point that he has made, the argument he is proposing, the proposition he is making, I think most people would recognise that this deal sounds too good to be true.

sections.label: Chief Valuer independence
sections.summary: The speaker states the Office of the Chief Valuer is independent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, let me put it beyond any shadow of doubt: the Office of the Chief Valuer is independent.

sections.label: Chief Valuer and BTO prices
sections.summary: HDB does not price flats to recover land and construction costs, the speaker says.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, the Member asks how to ensure that the Chief Valuer's valuations do not overly impact the cost of BTO flat prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have explained previously that HDB does not price HDB flats to recover the cost of land and construction.

sections.label: 4-room non-mature flat prices
sections.summary: Average 4-room flat prices in non-mature estates stayed fairly constant despite resale market rising 28% to 29%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, the average price of 4-room flats in non-mature estates has remained fairly constant before the pandemic in 2019 and last year, despite the resale market having gone up 28% to 29%.

sections.label: Subsidies adjusted for affordability
sections.summary: Subsidies and grants are adjusted from launch to launch by location and resale prices to keep BTO market stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But then, we have to apply the appropriate subsidies and grants in order to bring down these costs to an affordable level for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why from year to year, from launch to launch, the subsidies have to be adjusted – because of location, because of resale prices – to ensure that relative stability in the BTO market prevails.

sections.label: Taxpayer funding for home ownership
sections.summary: The overall taxpayer amount funding home ownership is public information and a huge figure with some breakdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The overall amount of money that Government uses as taxpayer dollar to fund home ownership is public information; it is a huge figure, with some breakdown.

sections.label: Cooling measures to moderate demand
sections.summary: The passage states that two rounds of cooling measures were made to moderate demand, with reasons articulated before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The reasons for this have been articulated before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why, amongst other things, we have made two rounds of cooling measures to moderate demand.

sections.label: Property market stability and affordability
sections.summary: The passage states reports suggest the property market is stabilising, the objective is stability, and BTO and resale affordability are being studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And if you have read news articles at the early part of this year, there have been reports that suggest that the property market is stabilising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It may be too early to draw definitive conclusions, but our overriding objective is to ensure stability in the property to ensure it does not run away from economic fundamentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On top of that, we continue to study how to ensure that both BTO and the resale market continue to remain affordable for different groups of Singaporeans at different income levels.
